title: Diodes and their uses
blurb: Choose the right diode (Zener, Schottky, PIN, varactor, LED) for a job and recognize each symbol.

E6B01.why: In reverse breakdown a Zener holds a **constant voltage** while its current changes: a reference.
E6B01.trap: Constant current and negative resistance belong to other devices.

E6B02.why: A Schottky's **lower forward drop** wastes less power as heat in a rectifier.
E6B02.trap: The advantage is low forward drop, not breakdown voltage or carrier retention.

E6B03.why: Forward voltage is set by the material's **band gap**: a bigger gap, a higher drop.
E6B03.trap: Junction capacitance affects speed, not the forward drop.

E6B04.why: A **varactor** is reverse-biased; its depletion width, and so its capacitance, follows the voltage.
E6B04.trap: A Zener is a voltage reference, not a variable capacitor.

E6B05.why: A PIN diode's wide intrinsic layer gives **low junction capacitance**, so RF is cleanly blocked when off.
E6B05.trap: Its job is switching RF, not high breakdown or high power.

E6B06.why: Fast and low-capacitance, a Schottky suits **VHF/UHF mixers and detectors**.
E6B06.trap: Constant-voltage reference is the Zener; negative resistance is the tunnel diode.

E6B07.why: Current heats the junction; **excess junction temperature** destroys it.
E6B07.trap: Excess inverse voltage is a separate failure, not current-caused.

E6B08.why: A Schottky barrier is a **metal-semiconductor** junction, not a PN junction.
E6B08.trap: A PIN junction has an intrinsic layer; that is a different diode.

E6B09.why: A point contact has tiny capacitance, so it works well as an **RF detector**.
E6B09.trap: Constant voltage is the Zener's job; a point contact detects signals.

E6B10.why: An **S-shaped bar** marks the Schottky. A Z-shaped bar is a Zener; a curved bar, a varactor.
E6B10.trap: The Z-bend symbol is the Zener, not the Schottky.

E6B11.why: **Forward DC bias current** sets the PIN's RF resistance, so it sets the attenuation.
E6B11.trap: Reverse voltage keeps it off; it doesn't vary attenuation smoothly.
